items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: when Miss Rae Ray Harrison and I played in Tokyo and all over Japan

ctx.x: Which, I wanted to say one thing here. The American musician is losing out, because the impresarios and the cabaret owners are too stingy to hire a band, but when we played -- when Miss Rae Ray Harrison and I played in Tokyo and all over Japan, they had bands that had eighteen pieces. And I know they don't have the money comparable to American cabaret goers and

theater goers. Now, they had everything there. Now, these boys are learning to play with big bands, while we are here -- the only thing that's saving the American musician against these foreign musicians, like in Japan, is because -- and some of the other Oriental countries -- is because they cannot im-provise, but they're good copyists. And they're good musicians. They can read and then they can copy a solo, an American solo, off the tape, or off the record. But they can't produce them themselves, yet. But, in…
